title: Delhi-based aerospace startup VEDA Aeronautics prepares bid for SAVITR, an airship-based surveillance platform
excerpt: Delhi-based aerospace startup VEDA Aeronautics is preparing a technical bid for SAVITR, an airship-based High Altitude Pseudo-Satellite (HAPS) platform designed to provide persistent surveillance for India's armed forces. SAVITR stands for Stratospheric Airship Vehicle for India's Theatre Reconnaissance. The proposed platform is intended to operate in the stratosphere and monitor large geographical areas for extended periods. Unlike conventional aircraft, which rely on aerodynamic lift, an airship uses buoyancy to remain airborne. This allows airship-based platforms to potentially maintain a presence over designated areas for long durations. Such systems could support surveillance along India's land borders and maritime approaches, providing information to defence forces over areas that require continuous monitoring. VEDA Aeronautics' HAPS collaboration The Delhi-based startup is also collaborating with UAE-based Mira Aerospace to offer HAPS technology in India. These platforms operate at high altitudes, bridging the gap between conventional aircraft and satellites. The HAPS offering is designed to provide what is known as a "geo-stare" capability, allowing the platform to maintain observation over vast geographical areas. Depending on its configuration, it can support defence operations, disaster management, border surveillance and strategic communication missions. The platform offers modular payload options, including electro-optical and infrared (EO/IR) sensors, communication relays and signals intelligence (SIGINT) systems. These payloads can support different surveillance, intelligence, and communication requirements. The HAPS offering is also designed for long-endurance, solar-powered operation and real-time intelligence gathering. By remaining airborne for extended periods, such platforms could provide persistent coverage without relying entirely on conventional aircraft or satellites. They could also serve as a cost-effective alternative to satellites for certain applications, depending on operational requirements and deployment costs. What is known about the SAVITR project? VEDA Aeronautics is currently preparing a technical proposal for SAVITR. However, its selection for the project has not been confirmed. The company has not disclosed the platform's final specifications, development timeline, or operational status. Details such as its dimensions, payload capacity, flight endurance, and power system have also not been confirmed for SAVITR. The specifications of VEDA Aeronautics' HAPS offering developed in collaboration with Mira Aerospace should not automatically be attributed to the proposed SAVITR airship, as the two have not been confirmed to be the same platform. Founded by Dipesh Gupta and Shagun Gupta in 2020, VEDA Aeronautics develops unmanned aerial systems and defence technologies for India's armed forces. If developed and deployed, SAVITR could offer another option for persistent high-altitude surveillance. However, its progress will depend on the project's selection process, technical development, and eventual operational requirements.
